## Summary

Salicylic acid by saponification of methyl salicylate (oil of
wintergreen) with aqueous sodium hydroxide, followed by acidification
with hydrochloric acid. This is sample data: the quantities follow the
textbook method but are not experimentally verified.

## Reagents

| Reagent | CAS | MW (g/mol) | Amount | mmol | Equiv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Methyl salicylate | 119-36-8 | 152.15 | 7.61 g (6.48 mL) | 50.0 | 1.0 |
| Sodium hydroxide | 1310-73-2 | 40.00 | 6.00 g | 150 | 3.0 |
| Hydrochloric acid, 37 % (12.1 M) | 7647-01-0 | 36.46 | 15.0 mL | 182 | 3.6 |

## Procedure

1. Dissolve the sodium hydroxide (6.00 g, 150 mmol) in water (60 mL) in a
   250 mL round-bottomed flask and let the solution cool to room
   temperature.
2. Add the methyl salicylate (7.61 g, 6.48 mL, 50.0 mmol). A white solid,
   the sodium salt of the ester, may separate at first.
3. Fit a reflux condenser and heat the mixture under gentle reflux for
   30 minutes, until the oily ester layer and any solid have disappeared
   and the solution is clear.
4. Cool the flask to room temperature, then in an ice bath.
5. With stirring, add the concentrated hydrochloric acid (15.0 mL,
   182 mmol) dropwise until the mixture is strongly acidic (pH 1 to 2 on
   indicator paper). Salicylic acid precipitates as a white solid.
6. Keep the suspension in the ice bath for 15 minutes to complete the
   precipitation.

## Workup and Purification

Collect the solid by suction filtration and wash it with two portions of
ice-cold water (10 mL each). Recrystallise it from the minimum volume of
boiling water, cool slowly and then in ice, filter, and dry the crystals
in air. Expected yield 5.52 g (40.0 mmol, 80 %).

## Characterization

Colourless needles, mp 158 to 160 °C (literature 159 °C). A solution in
ethanol gives a violet colour with a drop of iron(III) chloride solution
(phenolic OH).

## Notes

1. Methanol is formed in the hydrolysis and stays in the aqueous
   filtrate.
2. Add the acid slowly: the neutralisation is exothermic.
3. Salicylic acid is appreciably soluble in hot water, so wash the crude
   solid with ice-cold water only.

## Hazards and Waste Disposal

Sodium hydroxide and concentrated hydrochloric acid cause severe burns to
skin and eyes; wear gloves and eye protection, and add the acid in a fume
hood because of its vapour. Methyl salicylate is harmful if swallowed.
Salicylic acid is harmful if swallowed and causes serious eye damage.
Neutralise the aqueous filtrates before disposing of them as aqueous
waste.

1. Furniss, B. S.; Hannaford, A. J.; Smith, P. W. G.; Tatchell, A. R.
